fin_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me pull current bank balances for our monthly board financial report. We use {{vendor}} for startup banking, and you have configured API credentials for it. If any of the following are missing, ask me first: (1) confirmation that {{vendor}} API access is active, (2) which reporting date or period-end this report covers, (3) whether to include all bank accounts or only specific ones (e.g., exclude a reserved/restricted account).

Once you have what you need:
1. Call the {{vendor}} banking accounts endpoint (GET /developer/v1/banking/accounts) to list all bank accounts (checking, investment, managed portfolio) held by the business.
2. For each relevant account, call the balance history endpoint (GET /developer/v1/banking/accounts/{account_id}/balance-history) to retrieve the daily available balance, and identify the balance as of the report date I specified.
3. Compile a clean summary table with: account name/type, account_id, currency, and balance as of the report date, plus a total combined cash balance across all included accounts.
4. Flag any account with a stale or missing balance for that date, and note it separately.

Done looks like: a structured table (account name, type, balance, as-of date) plus a total cash figure, ready to feed into the burn rate and runway sections of the board report.

Report back to me with: the compiled balance table, the total balance figure, the as-of date used, any accounts excluded or flagged, and confirmation that the data was pulled directly from {{vendor}}'s API rather than estimated.

fin_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the revenue section of our monthly board financial report by pulling data from {{vendor}}, our payments platform. Use your configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s API/MCP tools.

Goal: Produce an accurate revenue summary for the current reporting month (and trailing comparison if available) covering gross charges, refunds, fees, chargebacks, net revenue, current balance, and payouts/deposits reconciled to underlying charges.

If you don't already know it, ask me for: the reporting period (start/end dates), the currency to report in if we operate in multiple currencies, and whether I want month-over-month comparison included.

Actions to take:
1. Query {{vendor}}'s analytics/report tooling to pull MRR or revenue metrics for the specified period, using a financial report template for board reporting if available.
2. Generate or pull a downloadable financial report (balance, payouts, revenue recognition) covering the same period.
3. If needed, read raw balance and charges data via {{vendor}}'s API to fill gaps — reconcile each payout/deposit to its underlying charges, itemizing fees, refunds, and chargebacks.
4. Cross-check totals across the analytics output, the generated report, and raw data for consistency; flag any discrepancies.

Done looks like: a clean summary table with gross revenue, refunds, fees, chargebacks, net revenue, ending balance, and reconciled payout amounts for the period, plus the source report(s) saved or linked.

Report back: the summary table, any discrepancies found and how you resolved or flagged them, and links/references to the underlying {{vendor}} reports used. Do not include any account credentials, keys, or tokens in your output.

fin_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the monthly board financial report. Your task is to pull expense data from {{vendor}}, our accounting system, for the reporting period.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in your configured credentials or environment, specifically:
- The reporting period (start and end dates) for this board update
- Confirmation of which {{vendor}} company/organization to pull from if multiple are connected

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s documented public API and:
1. Retrieve the Profit & Loss report for the specified period, broken out by expense category/account.
2. Pull the general ledger and trial balance detail for the same period in an open format (e.g., CSV or JSON) so figures can be independently verified.
3. Pull current accounts payable aging and vendor balances as of the period end date, so we can see what's owed and to whom.

Organize the results into a clean summary showing:
- Total expenses for the period, broken down by category
- Month-over-month comparison if prior period data is available
- Any unusually large or new vendor charges worth flagging
- Outstanding AP aging summary (current, 30/60/90+ days)

Save the raw pulled data (P&L, GL/trial balance, AP aging) as separate files or clearly labeled sections so they can feed into burn rate and runway calculations in the next step.

When done, report back to me with: (1) confirmation of the period covered, (2) the total expense figure and category breakdown, (3) any anomalies or flags in vendor spend or AP aging, and (4) where the raw exported data is stored so I can review it or hand it to the next step in the board report process.

fin_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me calculate burn rate and runway for our monthly board financial report. 

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (1) access to our accounting system (e.g., QuickBooks or Xero) via my configured credentials, or alternatively a CSV/export of the last 6 months of cash transactions, (2) our current cash balance as of the most recent month-end, (3) any known one-time or non-recurring expenses/income to exclude, and (4) the reporting period end date.

Once you have the data, do the following:
1. Pull monthly cash outflows and inflows for the trailing 6 months (or as many months as available).
2. Calculate gross burn rate (total monthly cash outflows) and net burn rate (outflows minus inflows) for each of the last 3 months, plus a 3-month rolling average.
3. Flag and separately note any one-time expenses that distort the trend.
4. Calculate runway in months: current cash balance divided by the average net burn rate (use the 3-month rolling average as the primary figure, and show a sensitivity range using the best and worst monthly burn in the period).
5. Note month-over-month trend direction (burn increasing, decreasing, or flat) and any notable drivers if visible in the transaction data (e.g., large new hires, vendor payments).

Produce a summary table with: month, gross burn, net burn, cash balance, and runway in months — plus a short narrative paragraph suitable for inclusion in a board deck.

Report back with the completed table, the narrative summary, and a list of any data gaps or assumptions you had to make (e.g., missing months, estimated figures). Do not send or publish this anywhere — just prepare it for my review.

fin_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me compile the draft of our monthly board financial report inside {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials: (1) which {{vendor}} workspace/team and parent page or database the report should live under, (2) the source locations for financial data (burn rate, cash balance, runway, revenue, and key KPIs) — e.g. specific {{vendor}} pages, dashboards, or connected data sources, and (3) the reporting month/period to cover.

Once you have this, do the following:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s AI Q&A capability to query recent workspace activity and pull the latest figures for burn rate, runway, cash position, revenue, and any tracked KPIs.
2. Use the AI drafting capability to generate a status-update style narrative summarizing progress, risks, and notable changes since the last report, citing the source pages/data used.
3. If available, incorporate or reference any existing dashboards/widgets or portfolio roll-ups relevant to financial or project health so the board report reflects a consolidated view.
4. Create a new page in {{vendor}} for this board report draft (using the create-page operation), structured with clear sections: Executive Summary, Financial Metrics, Burn Rate & Runway, KPIs, and Risks/Notes.
5. Populate the page with the drafted narrative and data, clearly citing sources/dates for all figures pulled.

Done looks like: a new {{vendor}} page exists containing a complete, well-organized draft board report with all required sections filled in with real data and citations, ready for human review.

Report back to me with: the link to the new page, a summary of what data sources were used, and any gaps or figures you could not find so I can fill them in manually.

fin_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT finalize or send) the draft monthly board financial report so I can personally review, edit, and approve the narrative before it goes to the board. This is step fin_003:n6 in the 'Board financial report' process.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: my accounting system export or spreadsheet (e.g., from QuickBooks, Xero, or a finance spreadsheet), current cash balance, monthly burn figures, prior months' data for trend comparison, key KPIs I track (e.g., MRR, ARR, customer count, churn, CAC), and any board template or format I've used previously.

Using this data, please:
1. Calculate/verify burn rate (average monthly cash outflow over the last 3 months) and runway (current cash balance divided by burn rate).
2. Summarize key financial metrics (revenue, expenses, cash position) and KPIs in a clear, board-ready format.
3. Draft a narrative section highlighting notable trends, risks, or changes since last month's report.
4. Flag any anomalies, inconsistencies, or missing data you notice in the source figures.
5. Compile everything into a single draft document (e.g., a doc or markdown file) organized with clear headers: Summary, Financial Metrics, Burn & Runway, KPIs, Narrative/Commentary.

Done looks like: a complete draft report with all sections filled in, calculations shown, and any data gaps or flagged issues clearly noted for my attention.

Report back to me with: the draft report itself, a short list of what you flagged or couldn't verify, and any assumptions you made. Do not send, distribute, or mark this report as final — this remains a human step, and you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the draft so I can personally edit and finalize the narrative before it reaches the board.

fin_003:n7.prompt:
You are helping me send this month's board financial report to our board members via {{vendor}}, the email platform I use. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) the finished board report content (financial metrics, burn rate, runway, and key KPIs) or the location of the draft/document to pull it from, (2) the list of board member email addresses to send to, and (3) any preferred subject line format or tone notes. Confirm you have access to {{vendor}} via my configured credentials/connection before proceeding.

Once you have the inputs: draft the board update email in {{vendor}}, using the report content to build a clear, well-formatted message (summary at top, key metrics table or bullets, burn rate and runway highlighted, notable KPI changes called out). Populate the recipient list from the board member addresses I gave you, and write a concise, professional subject line (e.g., 'Board Update — [Month Year]').

Prepare the email as a draft or scheduled send inside {{vendor}} using its documented email-sending capability, and show me the full draft — subject, recipients, and body — for review. Do not actually send or dispatch the email to the board. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before the message goes out, so once the draft is ready, stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft content, the recipient list you populated, where the draft lives in {{vendor}} (so I can review and send it myself), and any fields you were unable to fill in due to missing information.
